outline: 1844 Finding Unknown Sides Given the Area

examples.solution_text:
Use the $10\text{ cm}$ perpendicular height; the slanted side is not needed.
$\begin{align*}A&=\frac{bh}{2}\\55&=\frac{10b}{2}\\110&=10b\\b&=11\text{ cm}\end{align*}$

(a)
$\begin{align*}A&=bh\\A&=15\times8\\A&=120\text{ cm}^2\end{align*}$
$\begin{align*}120&=10h\\h&=12\text{ cm}\end{align*}$
(b)
$\begin{align*}A&=\frac{bh}{2}\\A&=\frac{21\times8}{2}\\A&=84\text{ cm}^2\end{align*}$
$\begin{align*}84&=\frac{12b}{2}\\168&=12b\\b&=14\text{ cm}\end{align*}$
Each new base uses its own perpendicular height, while the area stays the same.

Rectangle area $=10\times6=60\text{ cm}^2$.
Triangle area $=60\div2=30\text{ cm}^2$.
$\begin{align*}A&=\frac{bh}{2}\\30&=\frac{12h}{2}\\60&=12h\\h&=5\text{ cm}\end{align*}$

Smaller rectangle:
$\begin{align*}A&=lw\\21&=3w\\w&=7\text{ cm}\end{align*}$
Larger rectangle width $=7+8=15\text{ cm}$.
$\begin{align*}A&=lw\\150&=15h\\h&=10\text{ cm}\end{align*}$

Right part:
$\begin{align*}A&=bh\\75&=15h\\h&=5\text{ cm}\end{align*}$
Both parts have the same perpendicular height.
Left part:
$\begin{align*}A&=bh\\45&=5b\\b&=9\text{ cm}\end{align*}$

examples.derivation: Rectangle: 39.6 = 6w, so w = 6.6 m. Parallelogram: 84 = 12h, so h = 7 cm. Both follow formula, substitution and inverse operations.
55 = 10b/2; multiplying by 2 gives 110 = 10b, hence b = 11 cm. The diagram's slanted side has length sqrt(69 + 100) = 13, and its marked perpendicular height is 10.

Part (a): area = 15 × 8 = 120 cm², so the height to the 10 cm side is 120/10 = 12 cm. Coordinates give that side length sqrt(36 + 64) = 10 and its perpendicular altitude 12. Part (b): area = 21 × 8/2 = 84 cm²; 84 = 12b/2 gives b = 14 cm. Coordinates give BC = sqrt(132 + 64) = 14 and AF = 21 × 8/14 = 12. F lies beyond C; the added C–F extension correctly supports the external altitude.

Rectangle area = 10 × 6 = 60 cm². Triangle area = 60/2 = 30 cm². From 30 = 12h/2, obtain 60 = 12h and h = 5 cm. This combines the supplied area-relationship method with the taught triangle-height method.
Upper width = 21/3 = 7 cm. Lower width = 7 + 8 = 15 cm. Lower height = 150/15 = 10 cm. The diagram places the 8 cm extension between the upper and lower right edges.

Common perpendicular height = 75/15 = 5 cm. Left base = 45/5 = 9 cm. The dividing segment is parallel to the outer slanted sides, so both parts are parallelograms sharing the same perpendicular height.
